problem: Streaming LLMs still struggle to decide when to interact with incoming inputs, causing unnecessary latency and computation when using fixed interaction timing or external supervision.
approach: ProactiveLLM learns semantic sufficiency from partial inputs through mask-based streaming modeling and synchronized privileged self-distillation, enabling the model to make interaction decisions based on its own internal states without external teachers.
contribution: The method reduces interaction latency while maintaining generation quality on text and speech streaming tasks without requiring external annotations or stronger teachers.

problem: Existing methods for hallucination detection in LLMs rely on intermediate layers but lack principled, automated approaches to select the best layers across diverse architectures and tasks.
approach: FEPoID (First Effective Peak of Intrinsic Dimension) is a training-free layer selection criterion that identifies optimal layers by analyzing intrinsic dimensionality, combined with a truncation strategy to amplify hallucination-related signals.
contribution: FEPoID consistently identifies optimal or near-optimal layers for hallucination detection across question answering and summarization benchmarks with negligible computational overhead.

problem: Off-policy learning in large action spaces suffers from severe optimization issues in practice, even when using estimators with improved statistical properties.
approach: The paper shows that simpler weighted log-likelihood objectives enjoy substantially better optimization properties than current estimator-centric OPL methods, and proposes estimator-aware policy parametrization to mitigate optimization challenges.
contribution: Demonstrates that addressing optimization considerations explicitly yields competitive or superior learned policies compared to methods focused solely on improving estimators.

problem: Classical experimental design methods only target linear covariate balance, missing nonlinear structure that may matter for model performance and robustness.
approach: Extends the Gram-Schmidt Walk framework to directly control imbalance in nonlinear function classes by operating on Gram matrices, avoiding expensive explicit construction of nonlinear expansions.
contribution: Achieves nonlinear covariate balance with runtimes comparable to linear methods while preserving robustness against model misspecification.

problem: Mixture of Experts models struggle with continual learning on sequential multimodal tasks, facing rapid parameter growth and catastrophic forgetting when expanding to new tasks.
approach: CoPE introduces probe experts to dynamically determine where to add new experts, combined with a VAE-based Probabilistic Task Locator that matches inputs to task-specific components without task labels.
contribution: Delivers strong continual learning performance on the CoIN benchmark across eight VQA tasks with compact model size and no replay data.

problem: End-to-end autonomous driving methods fail to effectively unify future scene evolution and action planning, with inadequate sharing of latent states limiting visual imagination impact.
approach: DriveWorld-VLA tightly integrates VLA and world models at the representation level, using world model latent states as core decision-making states for the planner and enabling action-conditioned imagination in latent space.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with 91.3 PDMS on NAVSIMv1, 86.8 EPDMS on NAVSIMv2, and 0.16 3-second average collision rate on nuScenes.

problem: Finding second-order stationary points in differentially private stochastic minimax optimization has not been systematically studied, lacking unified treatment of empirical and population risks.
approach: Proposes a first-order method combining nested gradient descent-ascent with SPIDER-style variance reduction and Gaussian perturbations, using block-wise analysis to control stochastic variance and privacy noise accumulation.
contribution: Establishes high-probability guarantees for reaching approximate second-order stationary points with rates matching best known bounds for private first-order stationarity in both empirical-risk and population formulations.

problem: Inverse Lithography Technology for mask optimization relies on explicit physical metrics, limiting applicability of existing generative models that prioritize visual similarity.
approach: LithoGRPO integrates flow-matching with GRPO-based reinforcement learning fine-tuning, combined with a fast shot-counting algorithm for manufacturability evaluation, enabling optimization under physics-based constraints.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art ILT performance over both optimization-based and learning-based methods with efficient mask generation and 130× speedup in manufacturability evaluation.

problem: LLMs exhibit unintended code-switching in multilingual generation, yet the internal mechanisms causing this failure mode remain unclear.
approach: Introduces a circuit discovery framework to causally localize multilingual neurons and group them into interpretable circuits, revealing a language regime and semantic regime whose interaction causes code-switching.
contribution: Reduces code-switching rate by 20.8% through fine-tuning the identified language sub-circuit with minimal parameter updates (~0.019% of all neurons), offering mechanistic insights into multilingual LLM generation.

problem: KV cache in Vision-Language Models scales linearly with context length due to substantial visual redundancy, but existing cache eviction methods designed for language models degrade VLM performance.
approach: TGV-KV grounds visual information importance in textual guidance through Text-Vision Budgeting, Text-Weighted Ranking, and Text-Prioritised Retention policies that preserve text KV and rank vision importance via text-image attention.
contribution: Preserves 99.2% full-KV accuracy on VizWiz-VQA with LLaVA-NeXT while boosting end-to-end throughput by 52.6% at 5% retention budget.

problem: Backdoor and data-poisoning attacks achieve high success while evading spectral and optimization-based defenses, but the fundamental geometric mechanisms enabling this remain unclear.
approach: Uses kernel ridge regression to prove that clustered dirty-label poisons induce a rank-one spike in the input Hessian, identifying a near-clone regime where poison efficacy remains high while induced curvature vanishes.
contribution: Establishes an unavoidable safety-efficacy trade-off through input-gradient regularization and characterizes when backdoors are inherently undetectable, with validation across MNIST and CIFAR datasets.

problem: Multi-objective reinforcement learning struggles to balance presenting diverse policies with discovering the decision maker's implicit preferences without a priori knowledge.
approach: LatentMAS introduces a human-in-the-loop MORL framework that proactively learns DM preferences in real time and integrates this learning into parallel optimization, balancing exploration and exploitation.
contribution: Identifies policies aligned with human preferences on complex quadrupedal robot tasks with limited interactions, outperforming eight state-of-the-art MORL algorithms on MuJoCo and microgrid design tasks.

problem: Video retrieval systems remain context-agnostic at inference time, neglecting state and identity consistency needed for composing short clips into coherent long-form narratives.
approach: CAST is a context-aware adapter that predicts state-conditioned residual updates from visual history, introducing an explicit inductive bias for latent state evolution in video retrieval.
contribution: Improves performance on YouCook2 and CrossTask, remains competitive on COIN, and provides useful reranking signals for black-box video generation candidates.

problem: Online RL for flow-matching models requires full denoising trajectory rollouts for delayed terminal rewards, which is computationally expensive and suboptimal for learning.
approach: iGRPO replaces full-trajectory rollouts with single-step instant rewards assigned at each denoising step, enabling time-dependent reward signals that overcome limitations of time-independent terminal rewards.
contribution: Converges 10.2× faster than FlowGRPO while achieving higher final alignment quality across standard benchmarks.

problem: High-quality synthetic data from advanced AI models offers opportunities for statistical inference but poses risks when data quality is unknown, potentially degrading inference.
approach: GESPI wraps around any statistical inference procedure, leveraging synthetic data to boost statistical power while adaptively defaulting to standard methods using only real data when synthetic quality is low.
contribution: Error rate remains below a user-specified bound without distributional assumptions on synthetic data, with benefits demonstrated on AlphaFold protein structure prediction and reasoning model comparison.

problem: Unified multimodal models capable of generating intermediate visualizations as reasoning aids often fail to improve performance despite possessing the necessary textual reasoning capacity.
approach: MentisOculi develops a procedural, stratified suite of multi-step visual reasoning problems to evaluate models' ability to form, maintain, and manipulate visual representations in a goal-oriented manner.
contribution: Shows that visual thoughts do not yet benefit model reasoning, with models suffering from compounding generation errors and failure to leverage ground-truth visualizations, establishing necessary foundation to analyze and close this gap.

problem: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on text-based mediation for communication, creating re-encoding overhead and potential information loss in collaborative reasoning.
approach: LatentMAS enables pure latent collaboration among LLM agents through auto-regressive latent thoughts and a shared latent working memory that preserves and transfers internal representations without re-encoding.
contribution: Outperforms single agents and text-based MAS by up to 14.6% higher accuracy, reduces output token usage by 70.8%-83.7%, and provides 4-4.3× faster inference across math, science, and code generation benchmarks.

problem: The computational mechanisms underlying human episodic memory for retrieving experiences over extended timescales remain unclear due to limited mechanistic accessibility in long-term memory experiments.
approach: Uses long-context mechanistic interpretability to analyze how LLMs solve temporal order memory tasks, uncovering a one-dimensional temporal code reinstated during retrieval by a single time-reinstatement attention head.
contribution: Shows LLMs exhibit the same characteristic distance effect observed in humans on temporal order memory tasks, supporting temporal context reinstatement as a mechanism for episodic-like memory in both artificial and biological systems.

problem: Scaling language models to long contexts is bottlenecked by KV cache size, and current summarization-based compaction methods are highly lossy, substantially harming downstream performance.
approach: Attention Matching constructs compact keys and values to reproduce attention outputs and preserve attention mass at a per-KV-head level, decomposing the problem into efficient subproblems with closed-form solutions.
contribution: Achieves up to 50× compaction in seconds on some datasets with little quality loss, significantly pushing the Pareto frontier of compaction time versus quality.

problem: Multi-agent RL systems remain vulnerable to agent malfunctions, a critical failure mode that is underexplored in existing cooperative MARL methods.
approach: MARTA introduces a Switcher-Adversary mechanism that selectively induces malfunctions in performance-critical states, formulating a fault-switching game with a corresponding Q-learning scheme and contraction property.
contribution: Achieves large robustness gains of up to 116.7% in SMAC, 21.4% in MPE SimpleTag, and 44.6% in LBF, while significantly reducing failure rates under train-test mismatched fault regimes.

problem: Synthesizing high-quality, diverse multimodal training data autonomously for enhancing MLLMs is challenging without sacrificing either quality or challenge level.
approach: CADS operates through Collective Adversarial Data Generation (CAD-Generate) leveraging collective knowledge for diverse generation, and Collective Adversarial Data Judgment (CAD-Judge) for quality assessment, with Adversarial Context Optimization to encourage challenging samples.
contribution: R1-SyntheticVL trained on synthesized MMSynthetic-20K demonstrates superior performance on various benchmarks through adversarial synthesis.

problem: Cross-layer attention projection reuse improves optimization but creates a structural conflict: the first layer must act as both a stable anchor and an effective computational block.
approach: ExoFormer resolves this by learning exogenous anchor projections outside the sequential stack with normalized mixing of queries, keys, values, and gates using learnable coefficients.
contribution: Outperforms internal-anchor designs with the dynamic variant yielding 1.5x downstream accuracy points while matching validation loss using 1.5x fewer tokens than Gated Attention.

problem: Parallelizable RNNs for ultra-low power applications struggle with learning long-term dependencies and suffer from poor convergence stability and initialization sensitivity.
approach: CMRU replaces BMRU's state update with a cumulative formulation that restores gradient flow while preserving persistent memory through skip-connections across time.
contribution: Cumulative Memory Recurrent Unit and its relaxed variant αCMRU match or outperform LRUs and minGRUs on small model sizes with advantages on discrete long-range retention tasks while retaining quantized states for analog implementation.

problem: Voice deepfake detection models rely on representations from speech foundation models, but downstream finetuning has reached diminishing returns with limited generalization to unseen domains.
approach: Alethia combines bottleneck masked embedding prediction with flow-matching based spectrogram reconstruction as a pretraining recipe for a foundational audio encoder.
contribution: Significantly outperforms state-of-the-art SFMs on 56 benchmark datasets across 5 tasks with superior robustness to real-world perturbations and zero-shot generalization to unseen domains like singing deepfakes.

problem: Prediction-powered inference methods lack general ways to derive procedures with additional guarantees such as privacy, robustness, or validity under distribution shifts.
approach: Connects prediction-powered inference with conformal prediction by performing imputation through calibrated set-predictors to attain validity while achieving additional guarantees in a natural manner.
contribution: Provides the first general prediction-powered procedure for e-values that operates off-line, with advantages demonstrated on private and time-series data.

problem: Supervised fine-tuning can overfit expert data and degrade prior knowledge, limiting downstream RL which depends on a strong, generalizable initialization for exploration.
approach: Uses token-wise clipping to bound per-token updates on low-probability tokens, promoting progressive adaptation that fits new data while preserving general abilities.
contribution: Reduces out-of-distribution forgetting by 11.54% and improves final RL performance by 7.09% across agentic benchmarks, with smaller representational drift under clipping.

problem: Performing PCA on multiple probability measures lacks understanding of how convergence rates depend on the number of measures and samples per measure in a double asymptotic regime.
approach: Studies PCA in a double asymptotic setting with n probability measures observed through m samples each, deriving convergence rates for empirical covariance operator and PCA excess risk.
contribution: Establishes convergence rates of n^(-1/2) + m^(-α) and proves the dense-regime rate is minimax optimal for the empirical covariance error, revealing sparse to dense transition in convergence behavior.

problem: Video generators struggle with complex physical dynamics and lack fine-grained motion coherence, with existing approaches relying on external verifiers or additional training.
approach: Self-refining video sampling interprets the generator as a denoising autoencoder for iterative inner-loop refinement at inference time, combined with uncertainty-aware strategies to selectively refine regions.
contribution: Achieves over 70% human preference compared to default and guidance-based samplers with significant improvements in motion coherence and physics alignment.

problem: Understanding why Transformer attention heads attend to particular tokens remains unclear, limiting interpretability of attention mechanisms.
approach: Studies the query-key space using contrastive covariance methods to decompose it into low-rank, human-interpretable components where features align to produce high attention scores.
contribution: Identifies human-interpretable QK subspaces for categorical semantic features and binding features in large language models, enabling attribution of attention scores to identified features.

problem: Enforcing PDE constraints directly during diffusion's stochastic denoising is infeasible, and current methods trade off between PDE satisfaction and generative accuracy via Jensen's Gap.
approach: PIDDM applies physics-informed constraints post-hoc through distillation that enforces PDE constraints after training, enabling fast single-step generation with improved physical consistency.
contribution: Outperforms recent baselines like PIDM and DiffusionPDE in both accuracy and constraint satisfaction with lower computation, supporting forward/inverse problems and partial observation reconstruction.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has not been extended to 3D scene understanding and perception tasks in multimodal models.
approach: 3D-RFT extends RLVR to 3D perception through two stages: activating 3D-aware MLLMs via SFT, then reinforcement fine-tuning using GRPO with task-specific verifiable rewards like 3D IoU and F1-score.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on video-based 3D scene understanding benchmarks, significantly outperforming VG LLM-8B and mainstream models on VSI-Bench.

problem: Long-horizon forecasting of irregular multivariate time series requires balancing temporal structure fidelity with computational efficiency, as discrete methods distort via re-gridding and continuous models suffer from integration drift.
approach: Latent Laplace Diffusion models the target as a low-dimensional latent trajectory with stable modal parameterization via learnable complex-conjugate poles in the Laplace domain, enabling horizon-wide generation.
contribution: Improves over baselines in long-horizon forecasting and supports missing-value imputation by querying the same model at historical timestamps.

problem: Existing any-to-any multimodal approaches require training from scratch and cannot flexibly relate arbitrary modalities across diverse domains with pretrained models.
approach: MODUS uses a decoder-only architecture treating all modalities symmetrically, supporting arbitrary inputs and outputs without modality-specific heads or task pipelines.
contribution: Demonstrates strong out-of-the-box performance with flexible multimodal composition including chained generation through intermediate modalities and cross-modal consistency verification.

problem: How LLMs internally compute verbal confidence scores remains unknown, obscuring whether scores reflect just-in-time computation or cached retrieval.
approach: Uses activation steering, patching, noising, and swap experiments to reveal that confidence is gathered from answer tokens, cached at post-answer positions, then retrieved for output.
contribution: Shows cached representations explain substantial variance beyond token log-probabilities, revealing a richer answer-quality evaluation than fluency readout, with implications for understanding LLM metacognition.

problem: Centralized multimodal learning suffers from modality dominance where optimization gravitates toward easier modalities and spurious coupling that leads to overfitting incidental correlations.
approach: GCL applies a two-stage protocol with Selective Interaction (routing and auditing agents) and Consensus Formation (public-factor and aggregation agents) to govern multimodal collaboration.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and MIntRec benchmarks while mitigating modality dominance and spurious coupling across both regression and classification tasks.

problem: MoE Vision-Language Models incur prohibitive memory and computational costs, but existing post-training quantization methods overlook cross-modal differences and non-uniform expert contribution.
approach: VEQ introduces Modality-Expert-Aware Quantization using expert activation frequency and Modality-Affinity-Aware Quantization with token-expert affinity to guide calibration.
contribution: Under W3A16 configuration, achieves significant average accuracy gains of 2.04% on Kimi-VL and 3.09% on Qwen3-VL compared to previous SOTA quantization methods.

problem: Current meta-learning methods are constrained to narrow task distributions with fixed feature and label spaces, and key terms like 'universal' lack precise definitions, hindering comparability.
approach: Introduces TAIL, a transformer-based algorithm-implicit meta-learner with random projections for cross-modal encoding, random injection label embeddings for extrapolation, and efficient inline query processing.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on few-shot benchmarks while generalizing to unseen domains and modalities, solving text/audio tasks despite training only on images, and handles 20× more classes than training.

problem: SVD-based LLM compression struggles to allocate rank heterogeneously across matrices with different loss sensitivities, relying on expensive iterative pre-truncation optimization.
approach: Zero Sum SVD performs global singular component selection using activation whitening and first-order calibration loss estimates, with a zero-sum rule that keeps cumulative predicted loss change near zero.
contribution: Achieves consistent gains across multiple LLM architectures and diverse benchmarks without solving a rank allocation optimization, with optional lightweight correction via projected gradient updates.

problem: Standard on-policy distillation assumes a strong fixed teacher, unavailable in demonstration-only embodied control where the policy learns only on expert states without corrective signals.
approach: FA-OPD co-trains a Flow Matching teacher learned from demonstrations with a lightweight MLP student, providing reward and action distillation signals that enable generalization beyond demonstrations.
contribution: Beats strong baselines across six robot navigation, manipulation, and locomotion benchmarks with much stronger robustness under noisy or limited demonstrations.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models lack deliberation for complex or ambiguous scenarios, relying instead on instinctive fast decisions that lead to suboptimal or catastrophic actions.
approach: VLA-ATTC introduces adaptive test-time compute using uncertainty-based cognitive clutch, with a Relative Action Critic that identifies optimal actions via pairwise comparisons during deliberation phase.
contribution: Reduces failure rate of SOTA PI0.5 by over 50% on LIBERO-LONG benchmark through relative value estimation that simplifies learning and enables efficient sampling.
